extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED) staff, disciplinary counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Final order imposing reciprocal suspension of a registered patent practitioner based on discipline by another court; sets procedural findings, publication/notice requirements, and practitioner obligations during suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may impose reciprocal discipline upon a practitioner identical to discipline imposed by another jurisdiction pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline is filed by the OED Director requesting identical discipline; the Notice and Order provides an opportunity to respond and the Office acts pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for discipline: violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suspension is predicated upon being suspended from the practice of law by a Federal Court, here resulting from being suspended by the United States District Court for the Western District of Missouri.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice describes the underlying misconduct (in this case failure to prosecute a criminal appeal and failure to respond to appellate orders) as the factual basis for the § 11.804(h) violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and service requirements (certified mail and address of record)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Notice and Order must be mailed by certified mail to the respondent's address of record with OED; certified mail receipt numbers and delivery are documented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice was mailed by certified mail (receipt nos. listed) and delivered to respondent's OED address of record on a specified date; proper service and record of mailing are prerequisites to proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to respond within forty (40) days
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order provided Respondent an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by the other jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice informed respondent of the 40-day response period and the bases for opposing reciprocal discipline (the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1)). Failure to timely respond has legal consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adverse inference from failure to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent's failure to file a response leads to a determination that there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In light of no response, the Office concluded suspension for the same term was appropriate; failure to challenge the Complaint supports imposition of reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension terms and scope (identical discipline)
rubrics_metrics.description: When reciprocal discipline is imposed, the suspension before the USPTO is identical in term and scope to that imposed by the other jurisdiction (here: suspended for six months from practice of patent, trademark and other non-patent law before the USPTO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states the suspension is 'for six months' and that it applies to practice before the USPTO in patent, trademark and other non-patent matters, effective the date of the Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Notice of Suspension in Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a Notice in the Official Gazette containing the respondent's name, registration number, the fact of suspension, the governing regulation violated, and the underlying reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order includes a sample Notice of Suspension text (naming respondent, registration number, violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h), and describing underlying conduct) and points to the OED Reading Room link for disciplinary decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary agencies, courts, and public (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in states where the practitioner is admitted, to courts where known admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This notice obligation ensures communicating the USPTO disciplinary action to relevant jurisdictions and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties during suspension (37 C.F.R. § 11.58 compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 while suspended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order requires compliance with § 11.58 but does not restate the duties; practitioners must follow the statutory/regulatory responsibilities (e.g., notice to clients, handling of files) set forth in § 11.58.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from Customer Numbers and PKI certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO will dissociate the respondent's name from any Customer Numbers and the public key infrastructure (PKI) certificate associated with those Customer Numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As part of suspension, the Office takes administrative steps to remove practitioner access/association with electronic filing credentials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on applying for or obtaining a Customer Number during suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for a USPTO Customer Number, shall not obtain a USPTO Customer Number, nor shall her name be added to a USPTO Customer Number, unless and until she is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restriction prevents re-establishing electronic filing or access privileges until reinstatement; it is an affirmative condition tied to reinstatement status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory authority for discipline (35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary action is taken pursuant to statutory and regulatory authority, specifically 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order cites the enabling statutes/regulations as the legal basis for imposing reciprocal discipline and related administrative actions.
